column1: ### Victoria Universalis IV - canonical mod terminology.
### Tab-separated: id, english, category, definition, avoid
### `english` is the exact string used in localization/english. `avoid` records the
### mistranslation we have already seen or expect. Per-language decisions live in
### localization/glossary/<language>.tsv and, once locked, are never re-translated.

column4: definition
column5: avoid

column4: Spendable currency (0-1000) used to buy idea levels; earned monthly from literacy, schools, universities, administration and legitimacy.
column5: Not "insight" as personal perception or intuition. It is an administrative and scholarly point resource. Do not reuse the vanilla word for Innovation.

column4: Spendable religious currency (0-500) spent on Religious Programs and Religious Projects.
column5: Not piety as a personal virtue; this names a reform budget the state spends.

column4: Spendable cultural currency (0-500) spent on Identity Model changes and Cultural Projects.
column5: Mandate here is political authorisation, not an order or a command given to someone.

column4: Age-scoped currency earned from satisfied Age objectives and spent on Era Rewards; resets at each Age change.
column5: Not physical momentum and not "a moment in time".

column4: 0-100 equilibrium meter measuring how settled the relationship between state and faith is.
column5: CRITICAL: settlement means accord, arrangement, modus vivendi. It is NOT a place of habitation, a colony, a village, or "solving a problem". Every existing translation got this wrong.

column4: 0-100 equilibrium meter measuring how well the Identity Model fits the population.
column5: Social cohesion of the nation, not administrative unity of the state apparatus.

column4: The framework set by the Church and State law; one of four.
column5: Not "religious template". Model here is a constitutional arrangement.

column4: Religious Model privileging one state religion.
column5: Confessional refers to a confession of faith, not to confession as a sacrament.

column4: Tolerant Religious Model with weak conversion and higher migration.
column5: Use the established 19th-century civil-liberty phrase in the target language.

column4: Neutral Religious Model with full separation of religion and state.
column5: Not the separation or partition of the country itself.

column4: Religious Model of active secularisation.
column5: Names a state policy, not the beliefs of the population.

column4: The nationhood framework: Ethnic, Civic or Composite.
column5: Not "identity card" or personal identity.

column4: Identity Model built on one primary culture; strong assimilation.
Identity Model built on shared citizenship; strong migration and education.
Identity Model recognising constituent cultures under one crown or constitution.
column5: Composite is a political term (a state of several parts), not a material or "compound".

column4: One of eight permanent reforms available under a Religious Model, bought for 25 Piety Reform.
column5: A state programme of reform, not a broadcast schedule or computer program.

column4: State-targeted campaign running 0-100 progress under a Religious Model.
Religious Project of the Confessional State: converts part of a state's population.
Religious Project of Freedom of Conscience; never forces conversion.
column5: Outreach means public engagement and provision, not extension or expansion.

column4: Religious Project of State Atheism.
Countrywide or state-targeted campaign running 0-100 progress under an Identity Model.
Countrywide Cultural Project; a shared school syllabus.
Countrywide Cultural Project; common national symbols and ceremonies.
Cultural Project of the Ethnic Nation; assimilates a target culture.
Cultural Project of the Civic Nation; raises acceptance.
Cultural Project of the Composite State; permanently recognises a culture.
column5: Compact means pact or covenant here, never "small" or "compressed".

column4: One of 21 doctrine trees; a country may embrace up to seven over a campaign.
column5: Not a committee or a group of people, and not "group of thoughts". It is a school of doctrine.

column4: Taking an Idea Group into one of the country's slots; costs no National Insight.
column5: Not a physical embrace. Use the verb a state would use for adopting a doctrine.

column4: One of seven levels inside an Idea Group, written with a roman numeral, e.g. Idea IV.
column5: Keep the roman numeral exactly as in English. Do not convert it to a digit.

column4: The capstone bonus granted when an Idea Group reaches level VII.
column5: Not personal ambition; it is the completed doctrine's crowning effect.

column4: Umbrella word for the mod's idea system, used in UI headers and Journeys.
column5: Keep one word across the whole mod; do not alternate between synonyms.

column4: 24-month modifier applied by every idea purchase; it blocks the next purchase and cuts National Insight income.
column5: Strain here is administrative overload, not physical tension.

column4: The number of Idea Group slots a country has, earned permanently by total purchased idea levels.
One of seven country-specific bonuses unlocked at 3/6/9/12/15/18/21 purchased idea levels.
column5: Distinct from Idea Group and from Idea. Keep the three terms clearly different.

column4: One of two country bonuses granted at the start of the campaign.
The final country bonus, granted at 21 purchased idea levels.
Idea Group category header covering the economic doctrines.
Idea Group category header covering the social and political doctrines.
Idea Group category header covering the army and navy doctrines.
Production doctrine of factory owners and manufacturing scale.
column5: Not "industrious" and not "industrial" as a generic adjective; it names the industrialist class doctrine.

column4: Production doctrine of trade and merchant capital.
Production doctrine of banking, credit and minting.
Production doctrine of railways, ports and construction.
Production doctrine of mining and raw resources; mutually exclusive with Agrarian.
column5: Resource extraction, not "removal" or "excerpt".

column4: Production doctrine of the organised labour movement.
column5: The workers' movement, not work or labour as an activity.

column4: Production doctrine of farming and rural society; mutually exclusive with Extraction.
Society doctrine of universities and learned inquiry.
column5: Not the building named University; this is the scholarly doctrine.

column4: Society doctrine of administration and records.
Society doctrine of law-making and representation.
Society doctrine of health, insurance and social security.
Society doctrine of influence, infamy and relations.
Society doctrine of national homogeneity; mutually exclusive with Reformist.
Society doctrine of egalitarian reform; mutually exclusive with Nationalist.
Military doctrine of attack.
column5: Military offence, never "offensive" in the sense of insulting or unpleasant.

column4: Military doctrine of defence and fortification.
Military doctrine of fleets and shipbuilding.
Military doctrine of a trained standing army; mutually exclusive with Mass Conscription.
Military doctrine of the conscript nation; mutually exclusive with Professional Army.
Military doctrine of colonial expansion and tropical medicine.
Military doctrine of mobilised industry and propaganda.
One of the campaign's three eras.
column5: The historical era sense. Never a person's age or a duration.

column4: One of seven goals per Age; each satisfied objective pays Era Momentum every month.
column5: Not a military objective on a map.

column4: Bonus bought with Era Momentum; lasts only for the current Age.
A 15-year bonus, available once per campaign after securing five objectives in an Age.
column5: Use the established historical phrase.

column4: Golden Age variant favouring manufacturing and resource discovery.
Golden Age variant favouring education and prestige.
Golden Age variant favouring offence and war exhaustion.
Multi-year Journal Entry attached to an Idea Group, measuring real country conditions.
column5: Journey here is a sustained undertaking, not travel.

column4: One strategic Journey per Age offering three routes.
column5: Crossroads is a decision point; keep the singular sense even if the word is plural in form.

column4: One of the three paths chosen at an Era Crossroads.
column5: A strategic course of action, not a road or an itinerary.

column4: A decision event fired at fixed Journey progress.
Journal Entry that runs while a Religious or Identity Model change is absorbed.
Age 1 Era Crossroads.
column5: CRITICAL: Steam is steam power and the steam engine. It is never the Valve platform, and it must not be left in English.

column4: Age 2 Era Crossroads. Shares its name with Age 2 itself.
column5: Translate identically to the Age 2 name.

column4: Age 3 Era Crossroads.
Industrialist Doctrine Journey.
column5: The factory system as an industrial order, not a single factory's machinery.

column4: Academic Doctrine Journey.
column5: A community of learning; not a state named a republic.

column4: Professional Army Doctrine Journey.
column5: Use the military institution's established name in the target language.

column4: Panel tab: a sortable, filterable, paged table of every country's doctrine standing.
column5: Ledger is an accounting register or comparison table. Do not leave the English word untranslated; current files say "Doutrina Ledger", "Доктрина Леджер" and "主义 Ledger".

column4: Read-only doctrine section on the country panel, shown for any country.
Timed penalty after a cancelled project or a model change.
column5: Political reaction against a policy, not a physical recoil.

column4: Timed implementation penalty that blocks a repeat action.
A meter band: 75 and above, 26-74, or 25 and below.
column5: Not a rank or a league.

column4: The value a meter drifts toward each month, 20% of the remaining distance.
The 0-100 or 0-60 completion value of a project or Journey.
column5: Progress as a measured value, not progress as an ideology.
